text:
maya: quick question — PR https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/432 changes runtime/lib/ and infra/k8s/. CODEOWNERS lists @runtime-team for runtime/ and @infra for infra/, but most changes are tiny (rename var + one env name). who can approve/merge? do we need both teams to review or is there a fallback?
simon: can you paste the PR diff or a short summary? if it's truly a trivial rename we sometimes allow single-team approval, but infra config touches usually require infra ok.
maya: summary:
- runtime/lib/cache.go: rename cacheKey -> cacheKeyV2 (no logic change)
- infra/k8s/deploy.yaml: rename ENV_MYAPP_CACHE -> ENV_APP_CACHE (used by deploy script)
PR: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/432
infra-bot: CODEOWNERS check: owners required: @runtime-team, @infra. No approvals present. You can request an approver via `/request-approver` or add a reviewer.
alex: my take — add an infra reviewer for the k8s line and a runtime maintainer for the rename. if infra deems the deploy tweak safe we can merge after infra ack; runtime can rubber-stamp the rename.
zara: I can review the runtime rename today. if infra approves the k8s change, I'm fine to approve and merge.
simon: one note: if deploy.yaml rename affects CI/deploy scripts, infra might want a quick staging deploy + `kubectl diff`. flag that in the PR.
maya: done — added @infra-oncall and @zara as reviewers and added a rollback note and the `kubectl diff` step in PR description. @infra-oncall any objection to fast-track? :eyes:
infra-oncall: quick look — change looks safe. approving. please run `kubectl diff` against staging before merge. :+1:
maya: thanks — running staging diff now, will merge once diff is clean and there are no further objections. I'll monitor deploy and roll back if anything pops.
